name: shopping
description: PRD §6. The qualitative-instruction case: 'nothing ridiculous' has no enforceable meaning, so the compiler picks numbers and says so. Deliberately keeps the PRD's exact figures (max_transaction $900, step_up_above $1,250), which are internally contradictory — the coherence checker emits a warning about it. See DECISIONS.md, OQ-7.
intent_text: Get me a good hotel in Miami. Nothing ridiculous.

policy.summary: Book a Miami hotel for at most $900 per booking and $1,800 in total, with your approval required at or above $1,250.
compiler_notes: 'Nothing ridiculous' is not enforceable, so it was converted to explicit dollar limits that you should check.
Gambling is blocked even though many Miami hotels are attached to casinos; a resort charge coded as gambling will be denied.

assumptions: Read 'nothing ridiculous' as at most $900 per booking and $1,800 in total. Change these if they are not what you meant.
You will be asked to approve anything at or above $1,250, so you see the expensive end before it is charged.
Required the booking to be refundable, since you did not say it was final.
No hotel or booking site was named, so any merchant requires your approval.
Set this to expire in 24 hours — it reads as a request to act now, not standing authority.
